Kai: Heads-up: staging perf regressions after CUDA 12.4.1 + Triton 2.1.3 bump. Small-batch (1-4) p99 up ~18% on matmul-heavy models. CI perf job flagged it.
CI-bot: Perf regression detected: perf-smoke/staging #789 — p99 latency +18% vs baseline. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/perf/artifacts/789
Anya: Can you attach the tracer + triton kernel selection log so we can see which kernel swapped in?
Kai: Quick dump attached above. Short summary: Triton picked MatMulKernel_tiled_512x64 for batch=1 (used to pick 256x128). Also seeing repeated small cudaMemcpy stalls during KV prefetch overlap. Flame graph: https://prof.redwood/trace/1845553210
Ben: We saw something similar when 12.4.0 -> 12.4.1 rolled internally last month. nvrtc/codegen tweaks can nudge Triton's heuristics, and cublas algo priorities shifted too.
Maria: Is the matmul path here driven by Triton heuristics or downstream cublas selection? I thought we had more control via env vars.
Kai: It's a mix. Triton prefers fused/custom kernels when workspace fits; after driver bump the cost model changed and the heuristic now prefers the 512x64 tiling for our M,N,K shape which increases global reads for tiny batches. That reduces overlap with KV prefetch, so net latency goes up.
Sam: Can we force the older kernel selection via env override? e.g. TRITON_TILER_HINT=256x128 or set TRITON_DISABLE_TENSORCORE=1 for a quick check?
Anya: Plan: bisect across (A) Triton patch (2.1.3 -> 2.1.2) and (B) CUDA driver (12.4.1 -> 12.4.0). Need to know which one is dominant before a rollout hold.
Kai: Running quick experiments now: 1) revert Triton to 2.1.2 on canary 2) roll back driver to 12.4.0 on separate canary set. Will post numbers.
DevOps-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary-revert-triton-2.1.2 #790 at 20:45 UTC.
Kai: Results: revert Triton -> 2.1.2 recovered ~10% (p99 still +8% vs baseline). Rolling CUDA -> 12.4.0 on other canary recovered baseline fully. So primary regression introduced by CUDA 12.4.1 driver.
Ben: Good find. That matches the nvrtc/codegen shift hypothesis.
Maria: Short-term: pin driver to 12.4.0 on staging and stop rollout to prod until driver patch is validated by NV vendor. Also add a perf-blocker flag for driver upgrades.
Sam: I'll add a pipeline guard: any infra image bump that increases p99 >10% on perf-smoke blocks rollout automatically.
Anya: Long-term: add explicit kernel-selection logging to perf tests (diff chosen kernel name) and assert parity with baseline. Also add a small repro that isolates the matmul tiling choice so driver/vendor can reproduce locally.
Kai: Repro steps I'll post in the issue: minimal model + batch=1 + sequence length 64, run with --triton-kernel-log and cuda-mem-profiling. Quick workaround: set TRITON_TILER_HINT=256x128 or pin driver.
Kai: Opening tracking ticket PRJ-4567 with perf traces & driver bisect notes: https://redwood/issue/PRJ-4567
Ben: For next few hours let's pin the dedicated fleets and add a canary hold. Also notify support/CS so they can triage customer alerts.
Maria: I'll draft the rollback playbook and notify SRE rotation.
Sam: Added the CI gate.
Kai: Thanks everyone — will follow up with the profiler dumps and the minimal repro for driver team. :thumbsup:
CI-bot: Noted. Test run summary and artifacts linked in PRJ-4567.
